subject: zoology_2
question_text: Describe female reproductive system of a woman with the help of a labelled diagram.

mark_split.label: The six parts and the ovaries

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book pp.16-17, LAQ 4. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Figure revision (figure audit, 2026-09-05): a middle wall line was added on each side of the uterus so endometrium, myometrium and perimetrium each have their own target, and the cervical canal leader now lands in the lumen.

steps.label: The six parts and the ovaries
steps.why: The ovary is called the primary sex organ because it makes both the gamete and the hormones; everything else only carries or houses them.
common_mistakes: Calling the uterus the primary sex organ. The ovaries are.
Leaving out the hormones. Ovaries make steroid hormones as well as ova.
steps.memory_tip: Ovary, tube, uterus, vagina, vulva, glands — outside in, top down.
steps.margin_note: List all six parts first. That list is itself worth writing.
lines: The female reproductive system has 6 parts:
ovaries, fallopian tubes, uterus, vagina,
vulva and accessory glands.
Ovaries are the primary female sex organs.
They produce the female gametes, the ova,
and several steroid hormones.
A pair of ovaries lies one on each side of
the lower abdomen.

steps.label: Structure of the ovary
steps.why: The follicles sit in the outer cortex while the blood vessels run in the inner medulla, so an ovum has only a short distance to travel to the surface.
common_mistakes: Swapping cortex and medulla. The cortex is outer.
Leaving out mesovarium and tunica albuginea.
steps.memory_tip: Mesovarium ties it on; germinal epithelium and tunica albuginea cover it.
steps.margin_note: Four named coverings and layers carry this mark.
lines: The ovary is connected to the wall of the
abdominal cavity by a fold of peritoneum
called the mesovarium.
Ovaries are covered by germinal epithelium
and tunica albuginea.
The main body of the ovary is the stroma.
Its outer part is the cortex and its inner
part is the medulla, which holds blood
vessels, lymphatics and nerve fibres.

steps.label: The fallopian tubes
steps.why: The tube is not joined to the ovary, so the fimbriae have to sweep the released ovum into the funnel before it can be fertilised.
common_mistakes: Making the tube continuous with the ovary. It is not attached to it.
Placing fertilisation in the uterus. It happens in the fallopian tube.
steps.memory_tip: Infundibulum, ampulla, isthmus — funnel, wide part, narrow end.
steps.margin_note: Name the three regions in order and say where fertilisation happens.
lines: Each fallopian tube runs from near the
ovary to the uterus.
Its funnel shaped end is the infundibulum.
The edge of the infundibulum has finger
like folds called fimbriae, which collect
the ovum after ovulation.
The infundibulum leads into the wide
ampulla. The isthmus is the narrow part and
joins the uterus.
The fallopian tube is the site of
fertilisation. It moves the ovum towards
the uterus by peristalsis.

steps.label: The uterus
steps.why: The inner layer is rebuilt and shed every month, which is why the menstrual cycle is a change in the endometrium and not in the whole uterus.
common_mistakes: Naming two layers. There are three: perimetrium, myometrium, endometrium.
Giving the cyclic changes to the myometrium. They occur in the endometrium.
steps.memory_tip: Peri outside, myo the muscle, endo the lining that sheds.
steps.margin_note: Three layers plus the cervix and birth canal.
lines: The uterus, or womb, is single and lies
between the urinary bladder and the rectum.
It is a large pear shaped sac, highly
muscular and vascular, held by the
mesometrium.
The narrow part joining it to the vagina is
the cervix. The cervical canal and the
vagina together form the birth canal.
Its wall has three layers: outer
perimetrium, middle myometrium and inner
endometrium.
The endometrium undergoes cyclic changes
called the menstrual cycle.

steps.label: Vagina and vulva
steps.why: The vulva is a group name for the external parts, so the answer must list what it covers rather than describe one organ.
common_mistakes: Treating vulva as a single organ. It is the external genitals together.
Leaving out the hymen and the clitoris.
steps.memory_tip: Vagina is the tube; vulva is everything outside it.
steps.margin_note: Two headings. Keep each to three or four lines.
lines: It is a large fibro-muscular tube from the
cervix to the vaginal orifice. It is lined
by non-keratinised stratified squamous
epithelium and is highly vascular.
Vulva means the external genitals of the
female.
The vestibule has two openings: the upper
urethral orifice and the lower vaginal
orifice, often partly covered by a membrane
called the hymen.
The clitoris is a sensitive erectile
structure at the upper junction of the two
labia minora. It is homologous to the penis.
Mons pubis is a cushion of fatty tissue
above the labia majora.

steps.label: Bartholin's and Skene's glands
steps.why: Both glands lubricate, which is why each is homologous to a lubricating gland of the male system.
common_mistakes: Swapping the two positions. Bartholin's are beside the vaginal opening.
steps.memory_tip: Bartholin's beside the vagina, Skene's beside the urethra.
steps.margin_note: Position and function for each. Two lines each.
lines: Bartholin's glands are two glands slightly
behind and to each side of the opening of
the vagina. They secrete mucus that
lubricates the vagina, and are homologous
to the bulbourethral glands of the male.
Skene's glands lie on the anterior wall of
the vagina around the lower end of the
urethra. They secrete a lubricating fluid.

steps.label: Mammary glands
steps.why: Milk is made in the alveoli and then travels through wider and wider tubes, which is why the path has four named stages.
common_mistakes: Leaving the mammary glands out. They are one of the accessory glands.
Naming the ducts out of order.
steps.memory_tip: Alveoli, tubules, duct, ampulla, lactiferous duct — narrow to wide.
steps.margin_note: Follow the milk from where it is made to where it leaves.
lines: Mammary glands are paired structures with
glandular tissue and a variable amount of
fat.
They contain alveoli, which secrete milk
after the birth of the child.
The alveoli open into mammary tubules. The
tubules of each lobe join to form a
mammary duct.
Several mammary ducts join into a wider
mammary ampulla, which connects to the
lactiferous duct through which the baby
sucks the milk out.

steps.label: Diagram — female reproductive system
steps.why: The frontal view is the only one that shows both ovaries, both tubes and the single uterus in their true relation.
common_mistakes: Joining the fallopian tube directly to the ovary. There is a gap.
Leaving out the three layers of the uterine wall.
steps.memory_tip: Uterus in the middle, a tube each side, an ovary at each end.
steps.margin_note: Draw it large. Label at least ten parts.

elements.caption: Step 2 — the cervix and the vagina

insider_note: Six parts, so six headings plus the diagram. Number them at the top of the answer — an examiner marking eight points cannot find them in a paragraph.
